hook: Noam Shazeer joined Google in 2000, where he first worked on improving the search engine's spelling correction and helped develop the PHIL algorithm that became central to Google AdSense. Over the next two decades he moved into deep learning, co-authoring a paper on sparsely gated mixture of experts models in 2016 and then, in 2017, co-authoring Attention Is All You Need, where he designed the multi-head attention mechanism at the core of the Transformer. He went on to create Mesh-TensorFlow in 2018 for training large Transformers across many machines, co-authored the T5 model in 2019, and contributed to Google's LaMDA dialogue system. In 2021 he left Google to co-found Character.AI with Daniel De Freitas, serving as its CEO and building one of the first consumer chatbots built on Transformer technology. In August 2024 he returned to Google as part of a licensing deal with Character.AI, rejoining Google DeepMind's research team, and later co-led development of the Gemini model as Vice President of Engineering before departing for OpenAI in June 2026.
